title: Fleet priming playtest — weekly update (2027-05-25)
content:
Summary:

This doc captures the notes and measurement results from the fleet priming + soft-scaling playtest run May 18–24, with the weekly synthesis on May 25. The experiment focused on two coordinated levers to reduce cold-start tail latency during regional surges: (1) a small warm pool of prewarmed model containers (priming), and (2) soft autoscale policies that open short-lived burst lanes before official capacity provisioning triggers. The objective was to quantify p99 cold-start reduction, cost delta, and operational complexity across three regions (us-west, eu-central, ap-southeast).

Top-line results:
- p99 generation latency (cold-path) improved: us-west 1.9s -> 0.8s, eu-central 2.3s -> 1.0s, ap-southeast 3.6s -> 1.6s.
- End-to-end request success rate (surge windows) increased from 92.4% -> 98.7% (measured across test cohorts).
- Warm-pool steady-state cost uplift: ~4.1% of baseline GPU-hours when provisioning a 2% global warm pool; when restricted per-region the uplift ranged 2.6%–5.9% depending on regional reserve sizing.
- Cache/KV-hit improvements: requests served from primed KV snapshot rose from 12% -> 47% during early-surge minutes.
- Observability gap: current tracing doesn’t reliably tag soft-scale events with model-variant info; created INFRA-7810 to track.

Experiment design recap:
- Regions: us-west (primary traffic), eu-central (steady medium), ap-southeast (spiky test).
- Warm pool policy: maintain N prewarmed containers per model-type; eviction TTL 15m; start prewarm when queueing signal > 0.2 QPS baseline for 90s.
- Soft-scale policy: create "burst lanes" (short-lived pods with reduced scheduling priority) for 3m windows when predicted short-term demand spike detected by the workload predictor.
- Control cohorts: baseline (no priming), priming-only, soft-scale-only, priming+soft-scale.

Key observations and anomalies:
1) Priming effectiveness is model-sensitive. Smaller models (<=7B) had near-instant KV recovery and benefitted more per GPU-hour than larger 70B variants. For those larger models, priming helped but required larger warm pools or multi-stage priming to amortize activation time.

2) APAC region exhibited higher churn in preemptible capacity (preemptible rate ~1.7x global). This drove a higher warm pool eviction rate and required more aggressive lane replication; without replication, tail latency improvement degraded by ~40%.

3) Soft-scale alone reduced queue time but introduced transient scheduling pressure—observed 12% bump in scheduling failures on nodes with heavy disk IO (not GPUs). This indicates our soft lanes are colliding with non-GPU workloads; follow-up: constrain soft lanes to GPU-only nodepools (action item below).

4) Cache priming behavior: primed containers loaded a reduced KV snapshot (last 30m) rather than full-train checkpoints to speed startup. This improved startup from ~2m to ~18s for medium models, but completeness of the snapshot correlated with higher token-quality regressions in a small fraction of synthetic prompts — flagged for eval team.

Detailed metrics (weekly aggregate):
- us-west: 48h test window, peak simulated surge 4k QPS, warm-pool utilization 63%, primed-KV-hit 51%, avg GPU hours delta +4.3%, p99 cold-path 0.8s.
- eu-central: 36h window, peak 2.1k QPS, warm-pool utilization 58%, primed-KV-hit 44%, gpu hours delta +3.2%, p99 1.0s.
- ap-southeast: 24h focused window, peak 1.8k QPS, warm-pool utilization 47% (higher evictions), primed-KV-hit 38%, gpu hours delta +5.9%, p99 1.6s.

Action items (owners and target dates):
- (Diego) Constrain soft-scale pods to GPU-only taint/toleration sets; K8S PR and gating test - due 2027-05-30.
- (Sara) Add model-variant tag to tracing span for soft-scale/priming events; update tracing schema + dashboards - due 2027-06-03 (blocked on trace-schema review).
- (Luca) Run 48h follow-up for 70B models with multi-stage priming (cold->reduced->full) and report cost/perf inflection - due 2027-06-07.
- (Asha) Draft cost-accounting proposal for warm-pool billing (internal chargeback) and present at infra sync - due 2027-06-01.
- (Platform) Add eviction telemetry for preemptible nodes into capacity-scout; alert if eviction rate > 1%/hr for > 2h - due 2027-06-02.

Risks & tradeoffs discussed:
- Cost vs latency: warm pools reduce p99 but add steady-state cost. The small global pool (2% of active serving capacity) gave meaningful tail reduction at modest cost; larger pools have diminishing returns.
- Model quality drift: reduced KV snapshots lowered startup time but occasionally produced lower-quality outputs for edge prompts. Need a targeted eval set to measure regression surface before rollout.
- Operational surface area: soft-scale introduces more transient states (lane creation/eviction) which can increase alert noise and scheduling churn. Rollout should be staged to dedicated nodepools to minimize blast radius.

Decisions taken this week:
- Approve staged rollout: enable priming-only in us-west for 1 week on 2% warm-pool sizing. If SLOs hold for 48h, enable soft-scale in the same region constrained to GPU nodepools.
- Do not roll priming into ap-southeast until eviction telemetry is in place and warm-pool replication is validated.

Open questions for architecture review:
- Should warm pools be charged back to customer projects or central infra? (proposal to be discussed, Asha on docket for June 1).
- For multi-tenant nodes, what isolation guarantees do we require before soft-scale lanes are allowed?
- Can we compress KV snapshot further without quality regressions (v1: delta-compression + Bloom filter)?

Notes & references:
- Experiment tracking ticket: INFRA-7810 (linked).
- Implementation PR: github.com/redwood-inference/fleet-provisioning/pull/478 (warm-pool controller).
- Slack thread for anomalies: #infra-capacity -> thread "apac preemptible churn" (see messages May 20–22).

Next steps for next weekly readout (May 31 planning):
- Deploy warm-pool in us-west (priming-only) and start 48h SLO monitoring (Diego).
- Add tracing span enrichment and update dashboards (Sara).
- Prepare focused eval harness for medium/large models to measure quality delta from reduced-KV startup (Research team to partner; Luca to coordinate).
- Run cost-projection scenarios for 1%, 2%, 5% warm-pool sizing across projected traffic curves for Q3 (Asha).

Appendix — quick troubleshooting checklist for oncall:
- If warm-pool eviction rate spikes: check preemptible eviction telemetry -> increase replication or move to reserved nodes.
- If scheduling failures spike after soft-scale: disable soft lanes in region and check taints/tolerations.
- If quality regressions observed in primed starts: route traffic to control cohort and file an eval regression ticket.

Remarks: This playtest produced promising latency wins relative to cost with manageable operational complexity in the primary region. The follow-ups above focus on hardening telemetry and constraining soft-scale blast radius before a wider roll.

----
One-line summary for exec digest: Priming + soft-scale reduced cold-start p99 by ~50–70% with a modest ~3–6% GPU-hours uplift; next week we stage priming-only in us-west and harden tracing and eviction telemetry before expanding to other regions.
